original_question: Are the parallel identical machine problems P|r_j, p_j=p|sum w_j U_j and P|r_j, p_j=p|sum U_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?
target_in_paper: Section 4.3, Open Problem 7: Are P|r_j, p_j=p|∑ w_j U_j and P|r_j, p_j=p|∑ U_j fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?
correct_elements: The draft already identifies the exact open problem from the paper: the parallel identical-machine environment P, release dates r_j, equal processing times p_j=p, the two objective functions ∑ w_j U_j and ∑ U_j, and the parameter 'number of machines'.
missing_details: P means m parallel identical machines; because the notation is P rather than Pm, the number m of machines is part of the input and is the parameter.
The paper's default convention is nonpreemptive scheduling, since 'pmtn' is not present.
Each job j has an implicit due date d_j in addition to its release date r_j; p_j=p means that all jobs share one common processing time p.
In the weighted version, each job j also has a weight w_j.
U_j is the tardiness indicator: U_j=0 if job j is finished by its due date d_j, and U_j=1 otherwise; hence ∑ U_j counts tardy jobs and ∑ w_j U_j sums the weights of tardy jobs.
A feasible schedule assigns each job to exactly one machine, and each machine can process at most one job at a time.
Fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by m means that there should be an algorithm running in time f(m)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f, solving the exact optimization problem.
refined_question: Is each of the following two nonpreemptive scheduling problems fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number m of machines: given m parallel identical machines and jobs j with release dates r_j, due dates d_j, and a common processing time p_j=p (and, in the weighted case, weights w_j), compute an optimal schedule assigning every job to exactly one machine so as to minimize ∑_j w_j U_j, respectively ∑_j U_j, where U_j=0 if job j completes by d_j and U_j=1 otherwise?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is maximum weighted throughput (respectively maximum throughput) on m parallel identical machines with release dates and equal processing times fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by m, since minimizing ∑_j w_j U_j is equivalent to maximizing the total weight of jobs completed by their due dates, and the unweighted case is obtained by dropping weights?
justification: This draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact target: it matches Open Problem 7 in Section 4.3 rather than a broader neighboring problem. To make it fully stand-alone, however, the three-field notation and the FPT terminology from Section 2 must be unpacked: P is the parallel identical-machine environment with m part of the input; r_j denotes release dates; p_j=p means one common processing time; preemption is disallowed by default; and ∑ w_j U_j / ∑ U_j are the weighted / unweighted numbers of tardy jobs, with U_j defined using due dates d_j. Section 2.1.3 also gives the paper's explicit equivalent formulation in terms of throughput maximization. There are no algebraic ambient-field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions here; the hidden assumptions are scheduling-theoretic and parameterized-complexity-theoretic.
